title: Hobby router machine files start every new operation on Flood coolant, so a first post writes M8

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported on Discord (2026-11-21, relayed by Mike): a first-time CAM user generated G-code and found it turned on flood coolant and did a tool change, which they did not want. They did not know how to change it.

## What happens

`CoolantMode::machine_default` picks the default coolant for new operations from the machine's `coolants` list (`crates/app/tests/coolant_air.rs`, `the_machine_default_coolant_reads_the_coded_list`): Flood wins wherever it is listed. The shipped hobby machine files list Flood (M8) and Mist (M7), because the Grbl/grblHAL/TinyG controllers have those pins:

- `assets/machines/grbl-3axis.mch`
- `assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`
- `assets/machines/tinyg-3axis.mch`
- `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-2x4.mch`, `-4x4.mch`, `-4x8.mch`

So every new operation on these routers starts on **Flood**, and the first post writes `M8`. Most hobby routers have no flood coolant. The M8 pin is often unwired, or wired to something else (a relay, a vacuum).

## Expected

A machine file can state the coolant that new operations start on, separately from the coolant codes it can write. The hobby router files start new operations on **Off** and still offer Flood/Mist/Air for a user who has them. Industrial mill files keep Flood.

## Notes

- This changes the coolant words in posted G-code for new operations on these machines, so the safety floor makes it `effort:high`. Existing documents keep the coolant each operation stores.
- The user guide says Flood is the default (`site/content/guide/fundamentals/chips-and-coolant.md`). Update it to say the default comes from the machine.
- Not part of this issue: the tool-change half of the report. It came from posting with the default industrial mill instead of the Grbl machine; the Grbl post already writes an M0 stop, not M6.

Done means: a machine file can declare the default coolant for new operations (a test pins that the declared default wins over "Flood wins"); the Grbl, grblHAL, TinyG and Sienci AltMill files declare Off; a new operation on those machines posts no M7/M8 (a post test); the guide page states the rule.
